saw_lines: Organic cotton buyers compare certifications and fabric feel before picking a brand, then rebuy the same piece when it wears out.
So the sale is won or lost in the first line, where a buyer decides if the fabric suits them.
Your homepage shows $100, $250 and $500 prices, yet 0 of 28 ads mention price. Print one visible price on three new ads, beside the cost of replacing cheaper basics.

ads.source: Meta Ad Library, active ads, 7 Nov 2026
points: Your homepage shows $100, $250 and $500 prices, yet 0 of 28 ads mention price, so buyers cannot judge value before they click. Put one visible price on three new ads, beside the cost of replacing cheaper basics each year.

10 of 28 ads use claim words like clinically, cure and guaranteed results, which read as ad copy and get scrolled past. Rewrite them around what customers noticed, like how the fabric feels, and quote a review in each new ad.

7 of 28 ads are creator style posts run from your brand page. That reads as a real person and the voice gets lost under your brand name. Whitelist those posts from the creator account and cut three shorter variations.

7 of 28 copy ads open on the same “meet your new favourites” line, so anyone who sees you twice gets the same first sentence. Test two new angles against it, a fabric story and a care story, in equal batches.
